verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus and faithful in Christ Jesus:
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
verses.1:4: just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, for us to be holy and blameless before Him in love,
verses.1:5: having predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ for Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,
verses.1:6: to the praise of the glory of His grace, with which He graciously favored us in the Beloved,
verses.1:7: in whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,
verses.1:8: which He caused to abound toward us in all wisdom and insight,
verses.1:9: having made known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure that He purposed in Him,
verses.1:10: for an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth—in Him,
verses.1:11: in whom we also were allotted an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things in accordance with the counsel of His will,
verses.1:12: so that we who previously hoped in Christ would be to the praise of His glory;
verses.1:13: in whom you also, having heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation—in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
verses.1:14: who is the down payment of our inheritance, for the redemption of the acquired possession, to the praise of His glory.
verses.1:15: Because of this, I also, having heard of the faith among you in the Lord Jesus and that toward all the saints,
verses.1:16: do not stop giving thanks on your behalf, making mention of you in my prayers,
verses.1:17: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may grant you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him,
verses.1:18: the eyes of your heart having been enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance among the saints,
verses.1:19: and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of His strength,
verses.1:20: which He has worked in Christ, raising Him from the dead and seating Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
verses.1:21: high above every rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name being named, not only in this age but also in the coming one;
verses.1:22: and He subjected all things under His feet and gave Him to be head over all things for the church,
verses.1:23: which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all things in all.
verses.2:1: And you, being dead in your trespasses and sins,
verses.2:2: in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now working in the sons of disobedience;
verses.2:3: among whom we all also once conducted ourselves in the desires of our flesh, carrying out the wishes of the flesh and of the thoughts, and we were by nature children of wrath, just like the rest.
verses.2:4: Yet God, rich in mercy, on account of His great love with which He loved us,
verses.2:5: even while we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
verses.2:6: and raised us together and seated us together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
verses.2:7: so that in the coming ages He might demonstrate the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
verses.2:8: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves; it is God's gift,
verses.2:9: not from works, so that no one may boast.
verses.2:10: For we are His handiwork, having been created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we should walk in them.
verses.2:11: Therefore remember that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called "uncircumcision" by the so-called "circumcision" in the flesh made by hands,
verses.2:12: that at that time you were apart from Christ, estranged from the citizenship of Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the promise, not having hope and without God in the world.
verses.2:13: But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far away were brought near by the blood of Christ.
verses.2:14: For He Himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of the barrier, the hostility, in His flesh,
verses.2:15: having nullified the law of commandments in ordinances, so that in Himself He might create the two into one new man, making peace,
verses.2:16: and might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having put the hostility to death by it.
verses.2:17: And having come, He proclaimed peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near;
verses.2:18: because through Him both of us have access in one Spirit to the Father.
verses.2:19: So then, you are no longer foreigners and resident aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God,
verses.2:20: having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself being the cornerstone,
verses.2:21: in whom the whole structure, being fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
verses.2:22: in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.
verses.3:1: For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles—
verses.3:2: if indeed you heard of the administration of the grace of God given to me for you;
verses.3:3: by revelation the mystery was made known to me, just as I wrote earlier in brief,
verses.3:4: in light of which, as you read, you are able to understand my insight into the mystery of Christ,
verses.3:5: which was not made known to the sons of men in other generations, as it was now revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit:
verses.3:6: that the Gentiles are joint heirs, and members of the same body, and sharers together of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel,
verses.3:7: of which I became a servant according to the gift of the grace of God given to me according to the working of His power—
verses.3:8: to me, less than the least of all saints, this grace was given—to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
verses.3:9: and to enlighten all concerning what is the administration of the mystery hidden from the ages in God, who created all things,
verses.3:10: so that now the multifaceted wisdom of God might be made known through the church to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenly places,
verses.3:11: according to the purpose of the ages that He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
verses.3:12: in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through faith in Him.
verses.3:13: Therefore I ask you not to lose heart over my afflictions on your behalf, which is your glory.
verses.3:14: For this reason I bend my knees before the Father,
verses.3:15: from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
verses.3:16: that according to the riches of His glory He may grant you to be made strong with power through His Spirit in the inner man,
verses.3:17: that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts in love; having been rooted and grounded,
verses.3:18: so that you may have full strength to grasp with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
verses.3:19: and to know the love of Christ that goes beyond knowledge, so that you may be filled to all the fullness of God.
verses.3:20: Now to Him who is able to accomplish exceedingly beyond all that we ask or imagine, according to the power working in us,
verses.3:21: to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus to all generations of the age of the ages. Amen.
verses.4:1: Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthy of the calling with which you were called,
verses.4:2: with all humility and meekness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
verses.4:3: being diligent to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
verses.4:4: One body and one Spirit, just as you were also called in one hope of your calling;
verses.4:5: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
verses.4:6: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
verses.4:7: Now to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
verses.4:8: Therefore it says, "Having ascended on high, He took captivity captive; He gave gifts to people."
verses.4:9: Now what does "He ascended" mean, except that He also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
verses.4:10: The One who descended is Himself also the One who ascended far above all the heavens, in order that He might fill all things.
verses.4:11: And He Himself gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and some shepherds and teachers,
verses.4:12: for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ,
verses.4:13: until we all arrive at the unity of the faith and of the full knowledge of the Son of God, to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,
verses.4:14: so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, by the trickery of people, by craftiness aimed at the scheming of deceit,
verses.4:15: but speaking the truth in love, we may grow up in every way into Him who is the head, Christ,
verses.4:16: from whom the whole body, being fitted and knit together through every joint of supply, according to the working in measure of each individual part, produces the growth of the body for the building up of itself in love.
verses.4:17: Therefore I say this and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk just as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
verses.4:18: being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God on account of the ignorance that is in them, on account of the hardness of their heart;
verses.4:19: who, having become callous, gave themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of all impurity with greed.
verses.4:20: But you did not learn Christ in that way,
verses.4:21: if indeed you heard Him and were taught in Him, just as truth is in Jesus,
verses.4:22: that, regarding your former way of life, you put off the old self, which is being corrupted according to the desires of deceit,
verses.4:23: and be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
verses.4:24: and put on the new self, which was created according to God in righteousness and holiness of the truth.
verses.4:25: Therefore, having put off falsehood, let each one speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
verses.4:26: Be angry, and do not sin; let the sun not set on your anger,
verses.4:27: and do not give a place to the devil.
verses.4:28: Let the one who steals steal no longer, but rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to share with the one who has need.
verses.4:29: Let no corrupt word come out of your mouth, but only whatever is good for building up according to the need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
verses.4:30: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
verses.4:31: Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be removed from you, together with all malice.
verses.4:32: Rather, be kind to one another, compassionate, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ also forgave you.
verses.5:1: Therefore become imitators of God, as beloved children,
verses.5:2: and walk in love, just as Christ also loved you and gave Himself over for us as an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma.
verses.5:3: But sexual immorality and all impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints,
verses.5:4: nor obscenity and foolish talk or coarse jesting, which are not proper, but rather thanksgiving.
verses.5:5: For you know this for certain, that no sexually immoral or impure or greedy person—that is, an idolater—has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
verses.5:6: Do not let anyone deceive you with empty words, for on account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
verses.5:7: Therefore do not become partakers with them;
verses.5:8: for you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light,
verses.5:9: (for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth),
verses.5:10: discerning what is pleasing to the Lord.
verses.5:11: And do not participate in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather even expose them;
verses.5:12: for it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret.
verses.5:13: Yet all things, being exposed by the light, are made visible, for everything that is made visible is light.
verses.5:14: Therefore it says, "Wake up, you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you."
verses.5:15: Watch carefully, then, how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise,
verses.5:16: redeeming the opportunity, because the days are evil.
verses.5:17: For this reason do not become foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
verses.5:18: And do not become drunk with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit,
verses.5:19: speaking to one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making music in your heart to the Lord,
verses.5:20: giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God the Father,
verses.5:21: submitting to one another in the fear of Christ;
verses.5:22: wives, to your own husbands, as to the Lord,
verses.5:23: because a husband is head of the wife, just as Christ also is head of the church, He Himself being Savior of the body.
verses.5:24: Yet as the church submits to Christ, so also wives should submit to their husbands in everything.
verses.5:25: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself over for her,
verses.5:26: in order that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of the water in the word,
verses.5:27: so that He Himself might present the church to Himself glorious, not having a spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but so that she may be holy and blameless.
verses.5:28: In this way husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies; the one who loves his own wife loves himself,
verses.5:29: for no one at any time hated his own flesh, but nurtures and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the church,
verses.5:30: since we are members of His body.
verses.5:31: For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
verses.5:32: This mystery is great, but I am speaking concerning Christ and concerning the church.
verses.5:33: Nevertheless, let each one of you individually also love his own wife just as himself, and the wife must respect her husband.
verses.6:1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, because this is right.
verses.6:2: "Honor your father and mother," which is the first commandment with a promise,
verses.6:3: "so that it may go well with you and you will be long-lived on the earth."
verses.6:4: And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but raise them in the discipline and admonition of the Lord.
verses.6:5: Slaves, obey your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in sincerity of your heart, as to Christ,
verses.6:6: not with eye-service as people-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God, from the soul
verses.6:7: serving with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to people,
verses.6:8: knowing that each one, whatever good he may do, will receive this back from the Lord, whether slave or free.
verses.6:9: And masters, do the same things toward them, ceasing from threatening, knowing that the Lord of both them and you is in the heavens, and there is no partiality with Him.
verses.6:10: Finally, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of His strength.
verses.6:11: Put on the complete armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil.
verses.6:12: For our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.
verses.6:13: For this reason, take up the complete armor of God, so that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having accomplished everything, to stand.
verses.6:14: Stand therefore, having belted your waist with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
verses.6:15: and having fitted your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace,
verses.6:16: in all circumstances taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to extinguish all the fiery arrows of the evil one.
verses.6:17: And receive the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,
verses.6:18: with all prayer and petition, praying on every occasion in the Spirit, and to this end staying alert with all perseverance and petition for all the saints,
verses.6:19: and on my behalf, that a message may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
verses.6:20: on behalf of which I am an ambassador in a chain, so that in it I may speak boldly, as I must speak.
verses.6:21: Now so that you also may know the things concerning me, how I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make everything known to you,
verses.6:22: whom I sent to you for this very purpose, so that you may know the things concerning us and he may encourage your hearts.
verses.6:23: Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.6:24: Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility.

notes.1:4: Following the Greek punctuation here, "in love" modifies "holy and blameless before Him," though many connect it with "having predestined us" in v. 5.
notes.1:10: The verb translated "to sum up" (anakephalaiōsasthai) literally means "to bring together under one head" or "to unite."
notes.1:11: The passive verb eklērōthēmen ("were allotted an inheritance") may also be rendered "were appointed as God's heritage."
notes.1:15: Following the earliest Greek manuscripts, this text omits "love" (agapēn), repeating only the article ("that [faith] toward all the saints").
notes.1:23: The participle plēroumenou is middle or passive in form; it is usually taken in an active/middle sense ("who fills all things in all"), though some render it passively ("who is filled").
notes.2:1: The Greek leaves "you, being dead..." grammatically suspended without a main verb until God's action is stated in vv. 4-5.
notes.2:8: The neuter pronoun "this" (touto) points to the entire statement of salvation by grace through faith rather than to "faith" (feminine in Greek) alone.
notes.2:16: "By it" (en autō) refers to the cross, though it may also be understood as "in Himself" (Christ).
notes.2:21: Without the Greek article, pasa oikodomē ("the whole structure") can also be translated "every building" or "every structure."
notes.3:8: "Less than the least" renders elachistoterō, an emphatic Greek comparative built upon a superlative adjective.
notes.3:12: "Faith in Him" translates the Greek genitive tēs pisteōs autou, which some take as a subjective genitive meaning "His faithfulness."
notes.3:15: Greek uses a wordplay linking "Father" (patēr, v. 14) with "family" or "lineage" (patria).
notes.3:17: Following the Greek punctuation here, "in love" modifies "dwell," though many link it with "having been rooted and grounded."
notes.3:21: "Of the age of the ages" (tou aiōnos tōn aiōnōn) is a literal rendering of an emphatic Greek idiom meaning "forever and ever."
notes.4:8: Adapts Psalm 68:18, reading "gave gifts to people" rather than the Hebrew "received gifts among people"; "took captivity captive" renders a literal Greek cognate idiom meaning to lead away a host of captives.
notes.4:9: "The lower parts of the earth" can mean either the subterranean realm beneath the earth or, taking the genitive as appositional, the earth itself as the lower region below heaven.
notes.4:12: Interpreters debate whether the three prepositional phrases ("for the equipping... for the work... for the building up...") are coordinate purposes of the gifted leaders or whether the saints are equipped to perform the work of ministry.
notes.4:16: "Every joint of supply" is a compressed Greek phrase referring to every joint or ligament through which support and nourishment are provided to the body.
notes.5:2: The Greek text shifts from the second person ("loved you") to the first person ("for us"), a reading well attested in early manuscripts.
notes.5:5: "Of Christ and God" places a single Greek article before both nouns, which many grammarians understand as identifying Christ as God ("of Him who is Christ and God").
notes.5:14: An unidentified quotation—likely an early Christian hymn echoing Isaiah 26:19 and 60:1—introduced with the standard scriptural citation formula "it says."
notes.5:22: The earliest Greek text has no verb in this verse, carrying over "submitting" directly from verse 21.
notes.5:33: "Respect" translates the Greek verb meaning "fear" or "revere," echoing "the fear of Christ" in verse 21.
notes.6:6: The phrase "from the soul" (ek psyches) can be construed either with "doing the will of God" in 6:6 or, following the punctuation of the Greek text, with "serving with goodwill" in 6:7.
notes.6:15: The Greek noun hetoimasia ("readiness") can denote either preparedness to share the gospel or a firm footing supplied by it.
notes.6:16: The critical text reads en pasin ("in all circumstances"), whereas other manuscripts read epi pasin ("in addition to all" or "above all").
notes.6:20: The Greek noun halysei ("in a chain") is singular, likely referring to the single coupling chain binding Paul to a guard.
notes.6:24: The phrase en aphtharsia literally means "in incorruptibility" (or "imperishability"), conveying an undying, uncorrupted love for Christ; the earliest manuscripts omit "Amen."
